sources.entry: Seerr - Manage requests for your media library, supports Plex, Jellyfin and Emby media servers (fork of Overseerr). MIT Docker/Nodejs
Seerr | Media request management for Jellyfin, Plex and Emby

summary.one_liner: Seerr is a free, open source web application for managing media requests against a Jellyfin, Plex, or Emby library, and it is a fork of Overseerr.
summary.what_it_does: Seerr lets users request movies, shows, or individual seasons from your media library through a request UI, and lets admins approve or manage those requests. It authenticates against and imports users from Jellyfin, Plex, and Emby, and runs library scans so it can show which titles are already available. It also integrates with Sonarr and Radarr, supports PostgreSQL and SQLite databases, and offers granular permissions, watchlisting and blocklisting, notification agents, and email address changes for SMTP. The README says the interface is mobile-friendly and that the app has a local API documentation page. The README also covers migration guides for users coming from Overseerr or Jellyseerr.
use_cases: manage media requests for a Plex library
let family members request movies and shows
approve user requests for Jellyfin or Emby
integrate media requests with Sonarr and Radarr
how_to_run: Follow the installation and run instructions in the Seerr documentation (the README links to docs but does not include commands)
notable: Fork of Overseerr, with migration guide from Overseerr and Jellyseerr
Authentication and user import from Jellyfin, Plex, and Emby
caveats: The README does not include install commands; setup is delegated to the external documentation
Sonarr and Radarr are the only listed service integrations, with more described as planned
